The last 10 days show a steady decrease from 29.3°C to 27.7°C with no rain and moderate winds. Extrapolating this ~0.1-0.2°C daily cooling trend over the 7-day horizon yields the forecast.

micro.reasoning: Temperature has been declining gradually from ~29.8°C in early October to ~27.7°C by Oct 19, with a slight upward tick in the last few days. The recent trend shows a slow warming of ~0.1°C per day, likely due to seasonal transition and reduced precipitation. Forecast continues this gentle warming trend.

synthesis.reasoning: The macro forecast captures the dominant seasonal cooling trend from late September through October (30°C to 27.7°C), while the micro forecast identifies a recent short-term stabilization/warming signal in the last 3-4 days (27.7°C to 27.8°C). Given the strong seasonal signal over 50+ days versus a weak 3-day counter-trend, the macro trend is weighted more heavily (70%) but the recent stabilization suggests the cooling rate is slowing. A compromise forecast of steady 27.6°C reflects the transition from active cooling to near-equilibrium, with high uncertainty due to conflicting signals.
